11.K.
AGENDA
STAFF REPORT
AGENDA SECTION:
MEETING DATE: 1/20/2026
CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Affirm approval and appropriation from the General Fund reserve for emergency repairs on Fire
Engine #164 in the amount of $63,712.72 from Betts Truck Parts and Service of Fresno CA.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation:
That the City Council, by motion, affirm approval and appropriate from the General Fund reserve
$63,712.72 for the sole source repair of Fire Engine #164 from Betts Truck Parts and Service of
Fresno, CA.
Recommended Motion:
I move, to affirm approval and appropriate from the General Fund reserve $63,712.72 for the sole
source repair of Fire Engine #164 from Betts Truck Parts and Service of Fresno, CA.
BACKGROUND:
Fire Engine #164 was purchased in 2014 and has a current life cost of $233,443 and has
accumulated 103,286 miles as of the date of this report. In 2024, the engine required an emergency
engine replacement due to failure. The City Manager authorized to begin this repair under
emergency powers authorization in alignment with the City's Purchasing Policy to get the Fire Engine
in service as soon as possible for the City's Health and Safety of the public. As this is over a $50,000
cost, it is being brought to City Council for affirmation and appropriation of funds.
Recently, Fire Engine #164 has developed severe issues with the steering function on the vehicle.
City staff investigated the issue and determined that both lower and upper control arms are in need of
immediate replacement, along with the front suspension on the vehicle.
Although City staff has received fire-specific training on equipment, this is not a task that City staff is
either equipped for nor have the qualified experience for such an endeavor. Staff then reached out to
Betts Truck and Service to obtain a quote on parts and labor for repairs. Staff is recommended a sole
source procurement for the repairs of Fire Engine #164 due to the size of the vehicles, repairs
needed, availability of parts and expertise working on large-scale fire vehicles.
Fire Engine #164 has a replacement truck ordered. However, that vehicle will not be complete until
2027. Once the replacement truck arrives and is put into service, the existing truck #164 will be
placed in the City's Reserve Fleet and be available on an as-needed basis.
FISCAL IMPACT:
As these are emergency repairs, they were not budgeted for nor currently offset and therefore, would
be funded by the General Fund Reserve balance.

1. Betts Quote
2. Bett's Sole Source Justification

15.K.
AGENDA
STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 12/2/2025 AGENDA SECTION: CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Authorization for the City Manager to execute the purchase of an Internal Lift Screw Pump for
installation at the Wastewater Treatment Facility from Evoqua Water Technologies LLC, in the
amount of $1,325,000 and Appropriation of $450,000 from the Wastewater Fund (0362) to cover
approximately 30% of the purchase price.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation:
1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the purchase an Internal Lift Screw Pump from
Evoqua Water Technologies LLC of Thomasville, GA in the amount of $1,325,000; and
2. Appropriate $450,000 from the Wastewater Fund (0362) for approximately 30% of the
purchase price to place the order and to fund engineering expenditures through plan
submittal.
Recommended Motion:
1. I move to authorize the City Manager to execute the purchase an Internal Lift Screw Pump
from Evoqua Water Technologies LLC of Thomasville, GA in the amount of $1,325,000; and
appropriate $450,000 from the Wastewater Fund (0362) for approximately 30% of the
purchase price to place the order and to fund engineering expenditures through plan
submittal.I
BACKGROUND:
This item requests the City Council's authorization to begin the purchase process of a new internal lift
screw pump, which will replace Pump #1 of the Wastewater Treatment Facility’s (WWTF) headworks
primary internal lift screw pump array.
The headworks of the WWTF is the first step in the wastewater treatment process, where the City’s
entire conveyed wastewater enters the plant and undergoes primary treatment. The primary pumps
are comprised of internal lift “screw” pumps that lift the wastewater to begin the treatment process
through the facility. Preliminary treatment comprises screening raw sewage to remove inorganics
such as trash, grit, and sand.
City Council authorized the procurement of the Internal Lift Screw Pump (Pump #3) from Evoque
Water Technologies LLC at the December 3, 2024 City Council meeting. The WWTF headworks is
designed to accommodate a total of three internal lift screw pumps. Pumps #1 and #2 are currently in
operation and Pump #3 is currently being manufactured and once installed will complete the pump
array.
At the March 5, 2024 City Council Meeting, City Council authorized the procurement of an
emergency standby pump which serves as a temporary backup should the internal lift screw pumps
(Pumps #1 and #2) fail. At the July 2, 2024 City Council Meeting, City Council approved a
construction contract with W.M. Lyles of Fresno, CA for the installation of the emergency stand-by
pump. At this time of writing this report, the installation of the standby pump has been completed and
in use. This standby pump is critical to the operations of the WWTF should the primary internal lift
screw pump(s) fail resulting in a catastrophic spill. The standby pump will be activated upon the
malfunction or failure of one of the two degraded headwork primary pumps.
Also previously stated in the March 5, 2024 Staff Report, both existing internal lift screw pumps were
installed in 2002 and have a life expectancy of 20-25 years. In that report, Staff also apprised City
Council that the Wastewater Division had been experiencing a noticeable degradation in pump
efficiency due to the pump flight failure within internal lift screw Pump #1. Therefore, due to their age
and condition, an allocation of wastewater funds was made for this third pump and was included in
the Mid-Cycle Amendment to the 2024-25 Fiscal Year Budget approved at the July 2, 2024 City
Council Meeting. A replacement tube for internal lift screw Pump #1 was to be made later as a
separate CIP project, which is now budgeted in FY2027.
As mentioned above, this new internal lift screw pump tube will complete a series of (3) working
primary pumps. The headwork facilities was originally designed and constructed to include three
primary pumps and if approved this internal lift screw pump will replace the current Internal Lift Screw
Pump #1 within the wet well structure.
Procurement of this internal lift screw pump is a sole source purchase from Evoque Water
Technologies since they are the sole manufacturer and provider of the primary pumps currently in
use at the headworks facility.
The cost includes manufacturing, delivery, installation, field start-up services, and taxes. Note that
the attached quote is good through December 31, 2025, and could be subject to steel cost
fluctuations until the time the pump is released for manufacturing.
Staff recommends that the Internal Lift Screw Pump #1 be acquired at this time because of the
needed reliability and added redundancy needed should Internal Lift Screw Pump #2 fail, as it has
begun to further degrade, just as Internal Lift Screw Pump #1.
A minimum of two pumps are required because of the peak flows encountered especially during rain
events when flows can double. A single Internal Lift Screw Pump normally runs 24/7 while a second
internal lift screw pump helps supplement during rain events. Should either of the working pumps fail,
Pump #1 cannot by itself be used as a redundant pump to handle the average daily flows. Therefore,
it's critical to procure Pump Tube #1 since neither of the two pumps can be taken out of commission
and because of the one-year lead time it takes to manufacture, deliver, and install a replacement
internal lift screw pump.
FISCAL IMPACT:
Due to the critical need at the WTTF Headworks, approval of an appropriation in the amount of
$450,000 is recommended to begin the procurement process through Evoque Water Technologies
LLC. A 10% deposit is required to start the order and 20% due upon submittal of the engineering
drawings per the terms of the attached quotation. The total purchase amount is $1,325,000, but a
10% price increase is likely at the beginning of the year. 65% of the invoice balance will be due on
the day of delivery and final 5% following commissioning of the pump. The pump manufacturing
through delivery has an approximate 12-month duration.
The project is identified in the CIP as "Internal Lift Pump Tube #1" and budgeted in FY2027 in the
amount of $1,050,000. A final and firm price will be negotiated with Evoque and the balance due will
be appropriated as part of the mid-year budget review.
There are significant capital needs at the WWTF, therefore staff will continue to monitor the fund's
ability to handle critical capital needs. A review of capital fund needs and balances will be reviewed
during the budget process.

2. Headwork Internal Pumps and Wet Well

Recommendation: That the City Council, by motion, authorize a sole source purchase from QUINN
Power Systems and encumber $283,908 from the Water Well No's. 51 & 52 Capital Improvement
Project (CIP # 823637) 0391 Water Capital Funds in the amount of $283,908 to procure a Tier 4
500kW Diesel Generator to serve as a new backup generator for Water Well #52 and the Public

Recommended Motion:
I move to authorize a sole source purchase from QUINN Power Systems and encumber $283,908
from the Water Well No's. 51 & 52 Capital Improvement Project (CIP # 823637) 0391 Water Capital
Funds to procure a Tier 4 500kW Diesel Backup Generator for the new Water Well #52 and the

BACKGROUND:
Construction documents for the site facilities improvements for Water Well #51, located on
Grangeville Boulevard west of the BNSF railroad crossing, and Water Well #52 located at the Public
Works Corporation Yard are currently advertising for construction, with bid opening scheduled for
April 29th, 2025.
The City operates 12 generators to provide backup power to water wells and other city facilities.
These generators are all going through required regulation upgrades for compliance with air quality
requirements, and the older Tier 3 generators must be replaced with Tier 4 or higher. The city
participates in the SOURCEWELL Cooperative Supplier program, which is a cooperative purchasing
program that manages the solicitation requirements and combines the buying power of more than
50,000 government, education, and nonprofit organizations. The Cooperative Purchasing benefit is a
strategy where these multiple entities combine their buying power by sharing procurement contracts
and aggregating their volume to secure better terms, reduce costs, and streamline the procurement
process. By utilizing Sourcewell contractors and suppliers, the city is ensured to be getting the best
prices for construction materials quoted.
The City utilized Sourcewell Cooperative to request the quote for a QUINN provided Diesel
Generator. The city has a current maintenance contract with QUINN Power Systems to provide
monthly services to other backup generators. Therefore, it is recommended the purchase be through
QUINN to also minimize the inventory of spare parts for repairs and to provide consistent
maintenance for all city-operated generators.
The installation of the generator equipment will be done by the awarded contractor for the Water Well
#52 site facilities improvements, which is currently advertising for construction with bids to be opened
on April 29th, 2025.
QUINN Power Systems provides generators, including annual servicing and part for repairs for 12 of
the city’s critical generators for well, which is essential infrastructure for maintaining a constant power
source during outages.
The generators supplied by Quinn Power Systems are not only integral to ensuring uninterrupted
power to the city facilities but are also required to meet specific safety compliance regulations that
govern our operations. Quinn Power Systems is the only vendor capable of providing the specialized
equipment and support needed to meet these strict State and Federal requirements, including both
the equipment itself and the ongoing maintenance and parts supply.
Given Quinn’s proven history of reliable service and equipment provision to the city, we have
confidence in their ability to meet the unique needs of our well operations. Quinn is the only vendor
that offers the customized equipment necessary for our city’s operational requirements, and their
past performance has demonstrated that they can meet our timelines and safety standards
effectively.
Staff received a quote from QUINN Power Systems for a Tier 4 500kW Diesel Generator that will
provide backup power to the proposed Water Well #52 to be located at the Public Works Corporation
Yard, as well as provide backup power to the corporation yard building and facilities. The estimated
lead time for delivery upon approval is approximately 20 to 24 weeks. It is necessary to pre-
purchase the generator for the Water Well #52 project due to the long lead time.
The existing generator at the Corporation Yard was taken out of service several years ago due to it
being non-compliant with air quality regulations, and is legally not allowed to operate. Operating the
old generator would put the city at risk of fines if it were operated. Currently, the corporation yard is
operating without backup power facilities.
FISCAL IMPACT:
The FY 24/25 Capital Improvement Budget includes $693,709 and $2.4M in Water Capital and Water
Impact Funds, respectively, for the design and construction of Water Well #51 and #52 site facilities,
including a generator at Well #52. There are sufficient project funds available. Therefore, no
additional appropriations are needed at this time.
The quote from QUINN Power Systems in the amount of $283,908 includes delivery to the
Corporation Yard and excludes taxes and permits. Pre-order of the generator materials is necessary
due to approximately 20-24 week delays in shipment, which could delay construction completion.

STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 8/6/2024 AGENDA SECTION: CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Appropriate $66,251.55 from 20500000-825003 (Fleet Reserves Fund) and affirm emergency
approval of the sole source quote and authorize repairs for engine replacement in Fire Engine #164
for $66,251.55 with Golden State Peterbilt of Porterville, CA.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation: Appropriate $66,251.55 from 20500000-825003 (Fleet Reserves Fund) and affirm
emergency approval of the sole source quote and authorize repairs for engine replacement in Fire
Engine #164 for $66,251.55 with Golden State Peterbilt of Porterville, CA.
Recommended Motion: That, by motion, the City Council approves.
1. Appropriate $66,251.55 from 20500000-825003 (Fleet Reserves Fund)
2. Affirm emergency approval of the sole source quote from Golden State Peterbilt of Porterville Ca
for $66,251.55 to replace the engine in Fire Engine #164 and authorize the repairs.
BACKGROUND:
Per Hanford Municipal Code 2.48.060, the City Council has the sole authority to authorize purchases
exceeding $50,000, regardless of whether funding has already been appropriated in the adopted
budget. Additionally, purchases of $2,500.00 or more must have either formal or informal bids or a
sole source justification provided. The City Manager may approve emergency purchases if public
health and safety are in need, which was done in this instance for timely repair of an emergency
response apparatus.
Fire Engine #164 suffered a catastrophic engine failure earlier this month. Engine #164 was towed to
Golden State Peterbilt of Porterville Ca for evaluation. Golden State Peterbilt was selected due to
the responsiveness and estimated length of repairs. Golden State Peterbilt provided a quote to
replace the engine for $66,251.55 to install a rebuilt engine that comes with a 2-year, 200-thousand-
mile warranty.
Failure to authorize the repairs of Fire Engine #164 can result in long delays in service and risk to
public safety. Currently, Hanford Fire Department has a fire engine on loan from the California Office
of Emergency Response. This does not take into account any other issues that may arise with the
Fire Department's current fleet. Failure to repair will result in the reliance of surrounding agencies to
assist with calls for the City of Hanford.
Fire Engine #164 has previously been approved, by Council, for replacement and an order has been
placed with Pierce Manufacturing. Staff has spoken to Pierce Manufacturing, and they have provided
staff with an estimated delivery time of April 24, 2027, well outside the projected 3-month time frame
that Golden State Peterbilt has provided for the completion of repairs.
FISCAL IMPACT:
The Fleet Replacement reserves can absorb the impact of replacing the engine in Fire Engine #164,
at a cost of $66,251.55. $692,830.00 has been collected for the replacement of Fire Engine #164 in
2050000-825003 (Fleet Replacement Reserves) and the purchase of the replacement for Fire Engine
#164 has previously been funded and vendor paid in advance.

12.E.
AGENDA
STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 3/5/2024 AGENDA SECTION: CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Confirmation of pre-approval of an emergency purchase of a submersible stand-by pump for use at the Wastewater
Treatment Plant from Rockwell Engineering & Equipment Company in the amount of $78,259.13 and appropriation
of $79,000 from the Wastewater Fund (2073).
RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Confirm the City Manager's prior approval to advance the emergency purchase of a stand-by
pump from Rockwell Engineering & Equipment of Tustin, CA in the amount of $78,259.13; and
2. Authorize the appropriation of $79,000 from the Wastewater Fund (2073) for the procurement
of the pump.
Recommended Motion:
1. I move to confirm the City Manager's prior approval to advance the emergency purchase of a
stand-by pump from Rockwell Engineering & Equipment of Tustin, CA in the amount of
$78,259.13; and
2. To approve the appropriation of $79,000 from the Wastewater Fund (2073) for the
procurement of the pump.
BACKGROUND:
This item requests the City Council's confirmation of the City Manager's prior approval of the
emergency purchase of a stand-by pump to be installed at the WWTP Headworks (Installation will be
done by separate procurement process). The purchase is a sole-source purchase of a “Vaughn”
Pump, which has a 16 to 18-week lead time. This pump is critical to the operations of the WWTP
should the primary pump fail. Vaughn Pumps are exclusively used by the Wastewater Division. The
purchase will be in the amount of $78,259.13 based on the attached quote provided by Rockwell
Engineering and Equipment Co. The pump will be activated upon the malfunction or failure of one of
the two headwork pumps (see attached photo).
Staff requested the City Manager's approval to advance this purchase due: 1) the current critical
condition and deteriorated performance of one of the two main headwork pumps; 2) the potential
catastrophic sewage spill event that would result should both headwork pumps fail; and, 3) the long
lead time associated with the procurement of the stand-by pump.
The City Wastewater Treatment Facility utilizes (2) "Internalift" headwork pumps (screw pumps) to
convey wastewater from the sanitary sewer gravity system into the treatment facility for further
treatment. Failure of both screw pumps would result in a wastewater back-up in the sanitary system
and spillover out of the upstream manholes (approximately 8hrs. after failure). Both screw pumps
(installed in 2003, with a life expectancy of 20-25 years) are planned to be addressed during the
future plant upgrade, due to their age and condition.
Currently, the Wastewater Division has been experiencing noticeable degradation in pump efficiency
due to either a partial plug or pump flight failure of Screw Pump #1. This inefficiency results in not
having reliable redundancy in the event of a pump failure.
Therefore, staff recommends the purchase and installation of a stand-by pump, which will provide the
necessary redundancy and/or factor of safety should failure occur through either power outage,
control panel, or pump failure. A stand-by pump is also recommended as a faster and more
economical alternative. However, the facility will still require the repair and/or replacement of the
existing screw pumps during its next expansion or upgrade. Staff is closely monitoring the
performance of Screw Pump #1 as its pumping capability is diminished as noted above.
Due to associated long lead times, staff requested approval to purchase the equipment required in
advance. Installation will be procured by a separate bidding process when equipment is soon to be
delivered. This would drastically help speed the process, which also helps narrow the possibility of a
sewer backup.
Investigation into the issue has revealed that the wetwell facility requires a unique pump
characteristic available in pumps provided by Vaughn Pump Manufacturing/ Rockwell Engineering.
These pumps have historically proved successful in grinding or chopping down solids that are found
discharged into the City's sewer network. The price of this pump has been quoted at $78,259.13.
Other pumps in the industry are not capable of the abusive conditions particularly encountered in the
facility's influent wet well. Therefore, competitive bids are not applicable at this time.
FISCAL IMPACT:
Pre-approval of the Sole Source Justification made possible the advance purchase of the stand-by pump for an
amount of $78,259.13 to Rockwell Engineering, however approval to appropriate the necessary funds is still
required to fund the purchase.
Therefore, approval of an appropriation in the amount of $79,000 is recommended to fund the Purchase Order
issued to Rockwell Engineering & Equipment Company. The Purchase Order will be charged to the Wastewater
F und account No. 20730000-824612.

1. Attachment 1 - Rockwell Quote
2. Attachment 2 - Influent Wet Well and Headwork Pumps

14.H.
AGENDA
STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 1/16/2024 AGENDA SECTION: CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Authorization for the City Manager to execute a sole source purchase of a Pierce Fire Engine from
Golden State Fire Apparatus (Sacramento, CA) for $960,525 and appropriate $1,000,000 in the
General Fund contingent on confirmation of $1,000,000 in State grant funding
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation: Authorization for the City Manager to execute a sole source purchase a Pierce Fire
Engine from Golden State Fire Apparatus (Sacramento, CA) for $960,525 and appropriate $1,000,000 in
the General Fund contingent on confirmation of $1,000,000 in State grant funding.
Recommended Motion: I move to authorize the City Manager to execute a sole source purchase of a Pierce
Fire Engine from Golden State Fire Apparatus (Sacramento, CA) for $960,525 and appropriate
$1,000,000 in the General Fund contingent on confirmation of $1,000,000 in State grant funding.
BACKGROUND:
On June 20, 2023, City Council approved the FY24/FY25 budget, which included purchasing one type 1
fire engine. However, the City has received notice of award of a $1,000,000 grant for a Fire Equipment
from the State, thanks in large part to Senator Hurtado. This fire engine is needed in order to keep the
Fire Department's active engines in the most efficient working order. The long lead time of new fire
engines makes the timing of this grant welcome news.
Due to the pending grant, staff reached out to the dealer of Pierce Fire Engines which is the
manufacturer of existing Fire apparatus for the City. A quote was received and is good through January
31, 2024. The estimated arrival date for the new engine is 46 - 49 months upon order. This engine will
replace an older engine at Station 3. The City will be able to return to State OES an engine currently
being used.
The quote from Golden State Fire Apparatus in Sacramento, the closest Pierce dealer (there are two) in
California, includes pricing through Sourcewell a cooperative purchasing contract agency, which allows
participating municipal agencies to purchase equipment for a lower overall purchase price due to the
larger overall quantity and contract pricing (Sourcewell #113021, ID #252 - Member #85061). As part of
the confirmation process with the grant, staff will confirm if this type of procurement process complies
with funding requirements.
Pierce apparatus are currently used throughout the department. Continuing to utilize Pierce saves on the
training of Fire and Fleet personnel. Fire personnel routinely move between apparatus. Having a
standardized fleet limits unnecessary delays with equipment familiarization and training. Our Fleet
division is trained to repair Pierce apparatus, including motors, transmissions, and pumps. Having
different apparatus increases their training and equipment needs to maintain the apparatus and will also
increase the volume of parts stored in our already limited warehouse.
On February 1, 2024, Pierce will institute a 1.5% increase to all apparatus. Securing the purchase of the
engine before this date saves the City and prepaying for the engine saves $156,353.26 for a total
purchase price of $960,524.24, which is actually less than the engine ordered earlier this fiscal year due
to a larger prepayment discount.
FISCAL IMPACT:
Due to the pending $1,000,000 grant for a Fire Engine and Training Tower from the State, this purchase
will be fully reimbursed from grant funds. $39,475 of the grant will remain for a training tower. $1,000,000
appropriation in the General Fund will cover the expenditures that will be an equal offset by grant
revenues to be amended into the budget.
The City will need to pay for additional equipment upon arrival of the engine in about three years which
could be paid for from future fleet reserve funds.

Recommendation:
That the City Council, by motion, approve the sole source purchase of one (1) 2027 Front Load
Refuse Truck from Haaker Refuse of Tulare, CA in the amount of $497,506.79, and an appropriation
in the same amount from the Fleet Replacement Reserve Fund (0448)
Recommended Motion:
I move to approve the sole source purchase of one (1) 2027 Front Load Refuse Truck from Haaker
Refuse of Tulare, CA in the amount of $497,506.79, and an appropriation in the same amount from
the Fleet Replacement Reserve Fund (0448)
BACKGROUND:
The City of Hanford Refuse Division has been systematically converting its commercial refuse
collection routes from rear-load service to front-load service to improve operational efficiency,
enhance safety, and reduce long-term operating costs.
The current rear-load refuse truck, Unit #157, is a 12-year-old vehicle with 120,875 miles and a
lifetime maintenance and repair cost of $243,368. Having exceeded its useful service life, Unit #157
has become increasingly costly to maintain and is in need of replacement.
To support the City's ongoing fleet standardization efforts, staff evaluated replacement options and
determined that purchasing a front-load refuse truck from Haaker Refuse is in the City's best interest.
This purchase will maintain consistency within the existing refuse fleet, allowing the City to reduce
the inventory of specialized parts and supplies, simplify technician training, improve maintenance
efficiencies, minimize vehicle downtime, and lower overall life cycle costs. Replacing Unit #157 with a
front-load truck also supports the Refuse Division's continued transition to a more efficient
commercial collection system.
FISCAL IMPACT:
The City of Hanford Fleet Replacement Reserve Fund (0448) can fully fund this purchase.

STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 6/16/2026 AGENDA SECTION: GENERAL BUSINESS
SUBJECT:
Mid-Cycle 2026-27 Fiscal Year Budget Review and additional appropriation of $1,256,261 in the
General Fund, maintaining a balanced budget with cost reductions, deferrals and increased
revenues; and $10,629,688 across all Proprietary and Other Funds for necessary operational and
capital needs; and addition of three (3) Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) - Senior Fire Inspector, Fire
Inspector, and Senior Civil Engineer to the Personnel Master Budget that are offset by revenues and
project funding.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation: Staff recommends, by motion, the City Council approve an additional
appropriation of $1,256,261 in the General Fund maintaining a balanced budget with cost reductions,
deferrals and increased revenues; and $10,629,688 across all Other Funds for the Mid-Cycle
Amendment to the 2026-27 Fiscal Year Budget and the addition of three (3) FTE, Senior Fire
Inspector, Fire Inspector and Senior Civil Engineer to the Personnel Master Budget
Recommended Motion: I move to approve an additional appropriation of $1,256,261 in the General
Fund maintaining a balanced budget with cost reductions, deferrals and increased revenues; and
$10,629,688 across all Other Funds for the Mid-Cycle Amendment to the 2026-27 Fiscal Year
Budget and addition of three (3) FTE, Senior Fire Inspector, Fire Inspector and Senior Civil Engineer
to the Personnel Master Budget
BACKGROUND:
Council adoption of the City’s biennial balanced budgets for FY26 & 27 occurred on June 3rd, 2025.
A mid-cycle review, conducted after the first fiscal year, provides an opportunity for the City Council
to amend the second year of the biennial budget based on current year actual financial activity and
departmental requests reflecting anticipated operational needs. This review continues the principles
established by Resolution 20-29-R, which require the adoption of a balanced budget. Amendments
and new position requests are generally limited to core operational needs that support administrative,
public safety, and essential City services, and/or are offset by increased revenues or reductions in
expenditures. Consideration of current economic conditions, along with alignment with the City
Council's goals and objectives, remains a key component of the review process.
For all funds other than the General Fund, requests for new services or positions are evaluated on a
fund-by-fund basis to ensure sufficient fund balance is available or that the request is supported by
increased projected revenues or expenditure savings. Proprietary (Enterprise) Fund expenditures are
recovered through customer rates and charges that support ongoing operations.
The budget review process is further guided by the City Council's Strategic Planning Workshop held
on March 24, 2026, and the resulting 2026-2029 Strategic Plan. The Strategic Plan establishes the
City's long-term vision and identifies four key priorities: Quality of Life, Community Engagement,
Efficient and High-Performing Government, and Fiscal Sustainability. These priorities provide the
framework for evaluating departmental requests and allocating resources during the budget review
process, ensuring that funding decisions advance the City's strategic objectives while addressing
infrastructure needs, housing goals, regulatory requirements, technological improvements, and long-
term fiscal sustainability.
REVIEW OF GENERAL FUND REVENUES:
The primary sources of General Fund (GF) revenue are property tax and sales tax. In November
2024, City of Hanford voters approved an additional 1% transactions and use tax, which became
effective in April 2025. Although the additional 1% tax is considered General Fund revenue, it is
deposited into a separate fund to simplify tracking and reconciliation with the City Council approved
Measure H Expenditure Plan and in alignment with the 10-Year Expenditure Plan.
Chart 1 below illustrates the historical property tax and sales tax revenues received from FY19
through FY25, along with projected revenues for FY26 and FY27:
Sales Tax Overview
Sales tax forecasts for FY26 and FY27 indicate revenues are projected to potentially come in below
budget compared to the higher projections available at the time of original budget adoption. Since the
Mid-Year Budget Review, updated sales tax projections received in April 2026 have improved by
approximately $724,000 for FY26 and $885,000 for FY27. While these updated projections represent
a positive adjustment from the prior forecast, sales tax revenues may still come in below the amounts
included in the adopted budget. It is important to note that the majority of the improvement since the
Mid-Year Budget Review is attributable to stronger than previously projected sales tax revenues,
which shows there is volatility in projections.
The lower projections may be largely attributable to the impacts of inflation that have persisted over
the past several years. Sustained inflation can reduce consumer purchasing power, which may lead
to lower discretionary spending and, in turn, slower growth in sales tax revenues. Since 2024, the
Federal Reserve has begun lowering interest rates in response to moderating inflation, signs of a
cooling labor market, and broader economic uncertainty. Interest rate reductions are generally
intended to stimulate economic activity by making borrowing more affordable for businesses and
consumers. Current economic forecasts anticipate the possibility of additional rate reductions in
2027, which could support increased spending and a gradual improvement in sales tax revenues
over time.
While modest growth is anticipated in the coming years, prudent fiscal management and
conservative revenue forecasting remain important. Recent adjustments to the City's sales tax
projections have also been influenced by several one-time and structural factors. These include audit
findings identifying revenues that were incorrectly distributed to the City and subsequently adjusted,
temporary spikes in taxable sales related to large one-time projects such as solar installations that
have been removed from forecast assumptions, and declining taxable sales associated with fuel
purchases and vehicle sales within the City.
Property Tax Overview
Property tax is a stable and reliable source of revenue. Under Proposition 13, assessed property
values may increase by a maximum of 2 percent annually unless a property is reassessed due to a
sale or new construction. For the City, property tax revenues have helped offset declines in sales tax
revenue, allowing the overall budgeted revenue from these sources to remain relatively consistent.
There is typically a lag between development activity and the realization of property tax revenue due
to the time required for property assessment, tax collection, and distribution processes.
In addition to traditional property tax revenue, the City receives property tax in lieu of vehicle license
fees (VLF), a revenue source that replaced a portion of local government VLF funding with property
tax allocations. This revenue generally grows with assessed property values and development
activity, making it a stable source of General Fund revenue alongside property taxes.
As shown in the chart above, property tax revenues increased significantly in FY25 and FY26. This
increase is primarily attributable to the annexation of County property into the City between 2024 and
2025, which added hundreds of housing units to the City’s tax roll. As a result, the City is now
receiving property tax revenue from these homes. In addition, substantial residential construction
during this period added new assessed value to the tax base. Newly constructed homes are typically
assessed at higher values than much of the existing housing, which further contributes to revenue
growth. Home purchases have increased since 2023 despite higher interest rates. However, the
length of time on the market is longer, and prices have leveled off or fluctuated over time.
FY27 revenue projections have increased by approximately $150,000, reflecting continued growth in
assessed values, ongoing residential development, and updated allocation estimates.
The City is expected to continue experiencing property tax and property tax in lieu of VLF revenue
growth from FY26 to FY27 due to ongoing development and the annual allowable increases in
assessed values. However, the one-time boost associated with the recent annexations has largely
occurred, and the City is unlikely to see the same level of growth in the number of units being added
to the tax base. These revenues are therefore expected to continue growing, but at a more moderate
and steady pace.
Revenue Summary
Despite these projections, staff is not recommending any amendments to the budgeted revenues for
sales tax or property tax at this time. Since Mid-Year Budget Review, updated revenue projections
indicate that General Fund sales tax and property tax revenues have decreased by a combined
$652,000 for FY26. In addition, FY27 projections have decreased by approximately $95,000. Given
the significant fluctuations in current sales tax estimates and broader economic uncertainty, there
remains the possibility that revenue projections may improve during FY27. As such, staff
recommends maintaining the current budgeted revenue assumptions. However, in order to balance
the budget, reductions to fleet reserves are recommended and discussed in further detail below in
the Balancing the Budget section.
For FY26, the projected revenue shortfall could be offset through salary savings. These savings are
generated not only from existing vacancies but also from the City's conservative budgeting practice
of funding positions at the top step of the applicable salary range. Because many employees are
compensated below the maximum step, actual personnel costs are often lower than budgeted
amounts, creating ongoing salary savings throughout the fiscal year. Similarly, if FY27 sales tax
revenues come in below projections, these salary savings could offset a substantial portion, or
potentially all, of the resulting budget shortfall.
These circumstances further underscore the importance of budgeting personnel costs at top-step.
This conservative budgeting practice provides a financial cushion that helps absorb revenue volatility
and economic fluctuations when projections are difficult to forecast and subject to frequent changes.
During periods when revenues outperform expectations, these salary savings help strengthen the
City's financial position, while during periods of economic uncertainty they provide flexibility to
mitigate budget shortfalls without requiring immediate service reductions.
With respect to Measure H, updated revenue projections since the Mid-Year Budget Review have
improved significantly, increasing by approximately $1,124,000 in FY26 and $1,130,000 in FY27.
While these revised estimates represent a positive trend, projected Measure H revenues remain
substantially below the amounts assumed in the adopted budget. Similar to the General Fund sales
tax projections, staff is not recommending amendments to the Measure H revenue budget at this
time. Sales tax revenues have experienced volatility in recent years, making projections less reliable
and creating the possibility that revenues may improve as additional collection data becomes
available. However, given the current projected shortfall, staff is recommending reductions to certain
capital project appropriations, which are discussed in greater detail below in the Balancing the
Budget section. It is important to note that Measure H is still a relatively new revenue source, and
revenue projections are expected to become more reliable over time as several years of actual
receipt data are collected and analyzed.
BALANCING THE BUDGET:
General Fund
Excluding the decreased projections for FY27 General Fund revenues which are offset by salary
savings, the net change to the General Fund is balanced. The total request for additional
appropriation in the General Fund is $1,256,261. The actual impact on the General Fund will be
slightly lower due to the City’s service allocation process. Divisions within the General Fund that
provide services to other funds/divisions are able to allocate and recover a portion of their costs
through reimbursements. Of the $399,134 appropriation requested by the City Council, City
Manager-City Clerk, Human Resources, Utilities and Engineering, a portion of at least approximately
$57,000 will be allocated to funds outside the general fund based on services provided, or staff time
related to projects. This allocation process will reduce the overall cost burden on the General Fund.
Staff evaluated a variety of available strategies to achieve a balanced budget and is recommending a
decrease to the annual fleet replacement reserve contribution of approximately 44% or $621,347
across all GF departments. This approach was selected because the Fleet Replacement Internal
Service Fund currently maintains a healthy fund balance that can absorb a temporary reduction in
annual contributions without impacting near-term vehicle replacement needs. As a result, the City
can maintain current service levels while achieving a balanced budget. This is proposed only for
FY27 and is not an ongoing strategy for maintaining a balanced budget.
Staff will continue to monitor revenues and expenditures throughout the fiscal year. As part of the
Mid-Year Budget Review in March 2027, staff will evaluate the current additional appropriation
requests and corresponding revenue adjustments and may recommend expenditure reductions if
anticipated revenues are not realized. Conversely, if revenue trends improve beyond current
projections, staff may reassess and potentially restore Fleet Replacement Reserve contributions to
their original funding levels.
Measure H
Measure H expenses consists of salaries and benefits and capital improvement projects. Staff does
not recommend eliminating employee positions, as personnel reductions would not sufficiently
address the projected revenue shortfall and would impact service levels.
Instead, staff reviewed Measure H funded capital projects and identified the Streets Pavement

STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE: 8/19/2025 AGENDA SECTION: CONSENT CALENDAR
SUBJECT:
Approve Sole Source Contract for JR Construction Inc. in the amount of $128,479.53 for Phase Two
of Community Development Remodel Project (CIP 825620) included in Capital Improvement Plan for
Fiscal Year 2025/26.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the expenditure of previously
appropriated funds and award contract to JR Scott Construction Inc for a not-to-exceed amount of
$128,479.53 for the second phase of the Community Development Remodel Capital Improvement
Project (CIP 825620), as outlined in the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Plan.
Recommended Motion: I make a motion to authorize the expenditure of previously appropriated
funds and award contract to JR Scott Construction Inc for a not-to-exceed amount of $128,479.53 for
the second phase of the Community Development Remodel Capital Improvement Project (CIP
825620), as outlined in the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Plan.
BACKGROUND:
On May 20, 2025, the City Council approved an advance appropriation of $610,000 for the
Community Development Remodel project. The project is a multi-funded initiative included in the FY
2025/26 Capital Improvement Plan, designed to modernize the Community Development Department
workspace to improve operational efficiency, and staff functionality.
PHASE ONE
The initial phase of the remodel, close to completion, included:
• Relocating the public service counter
• Demolition and replacement of four cubicle spaces with more functional configurations
• Purchase of desks
• Addition of two new workspaces
• Relocation of the Building Official’s office door
• Removal of wallpaper, addition of wall texture, and painting throughout the area
Estimated cost for Phase One: $66,946.72
PHASE TWO
Staff is now seeking authorization to proceed with the second phase of the remodel, which will bring
project costs above $50,000, requiring City Council approval. This phase is focused on further
improving workspace efficiency and accommodating department needs, and includes:
• Demolition and reconfiguration of existing workspaces
• Construction of a new meeting room
• Creation of dedicated space for copier and supplies storage
• Addition of an employee-use area, including space for a refrigerator, microwave, and sink
Estimated cost for Phase Two: $165,327.48
Advancing to the second phase will complete the remodel in alignment with the goals presented
during the CIP review and will provide necessary functional improvements to support both staff
operations and customer service delivery.
SOLE SOURCE
To ensure continuity in project execution and maintain consistency in design and quality construction,
staff is recommending a sole source contract with JR Scott Construction Inc, the same contractor that
successfully completed the first phase of the remodel. This contractor is familiar with the facility
layout, project requirements, and prior work completed, which will help minimize disruption and avoid
potential delays.
In seeking additional bids, staff contacted two other qualified contractors; however, both indicated
they were unable to submit proposals due to existing workload commitments. Given the time-
sensitive nature of the project and the proven performance of the Phase One contractor, proceeding
on a sole source basis is in the City’s best interest.
FISCAL IMPACT:
No additional appropriation is requested at this time. Funding for the second phase is included in the
$610,000 previously appropriated. The project is multi-funded as follows:
• $150,000 – General Fund (Fund 0001)
• $460,000 – Building Safety Fund (Fund 0340)

SUBJECT:
Approval of a sole source procurement of three (3) Ford F-150 pickup trucks, two (2) Ford F-150 Lightning EV
pickup trucks and five (5) Dodge Durango Pursuit Vehicles from National Auto Fleet Group of Watsonville, CA,
under Sourcewell Contract 091521-NAF, in the amount of $574,881.68 and approve the upfitting of said vehicles by
Cooks Communications of Fresno, CA, in the amount of $343,094.13, for a total expenditure of $917,975.81 to be
funded by Measure H.
RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation:
That the City Council authorize procurement of three (3) F-150, two (2) F-150 Lightning EV pickup trucks and five
(5) Dodge Durango Pursuit Vehicles with upfitting from National Auto Fleet Group (vehicle) and Cook
Communications (upfitting)
Recommended Motion:
That by motion, the City Council authorize procurement of three (3) F-150, two (2) F-150 Lightning EV pickup trucks
and five (5) Dodge Durango Pursuit Vehicles with upfitting from National Auto Fleet Group (vehicle) and Cook
Communications (upfitting)
BACKGROUND:
In 2024, the citizens of Hanford approved Measure H. A portion of Measure H calls out a specific
expenditure plan that was approved overwhelmingly by the Measure H Revenue Committee. Within
the expenditure plan, it calls out for the hiring of several additional officers for Hanford PD, including
HART officers, and additional patrol officers. The purchase of these vehicles will provide the support
needed for the daily activities of newly hired officers.
The City of Hanford Fleets Services and the Hanford Police Department (PD) have worked closely in
an effort to balance the needs of the department with the requirements on vehicle emissions. Due to
the emission requirements, it was determined that the purchase of the F-150 Lightning EV pickups
will allow us to maintain a plan of compliance, avoiding any potential hefty fines from the California
Airboard and serve the needs of the community and Hanford PD.
A sole source authorization is recommended for the acquisition of both gas-powered vehicles and
electric F-150 trucks. Based on the delivery timelines, it is critical to limit the amount of time it takes
to get these vehicles operational. Local vendors were contacted. Dodge was unable to provide a
local quote. The local Ford vendor will not have any trucks in stock for a minimum of 6-8 months, as
opposed to the vendor recommended that can have the trucks in as little as two months. The city will
continue to seek out local purchases as available. By going with National Auto Fleet group, the
timeline for a vehicle on the street is reduced by a projected 4-6 months, unfitting of vehicles may
take 1-2 months. It is in the best interest of the city to pursue more timely options to get these
v ehicles in service as soon as possible.
FISCAL IMPACT:
Measure H can fully support this purchase and an appropriation is in place for fiscal year 2025/2026
for these vehicles.
